text.p: VIENNA, July 23 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Wednesday are:

- Tension is high between the ruling coalition government partners the Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party ahead of the presentation of the budgets for 1998 and 1999 as the proposals leave some questions unanswered.
- The Social Democrats' army spokesman says he can imagine Austria having a professional army and calls for a reduction in numbers of Austria's army.
- The merged bank of Die Erste and GiroCredit will be called Erste Bank der Oesterreichischen Sparkassen AG.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger, in his budgets for 1998 and 1999, is taking on more debts than originally planned in order to finance social benefit spending.
- Novomatic wants to buy the postal savings bank's (PSK) 34 percent stake in Austria's lottery company.
- Around 200 Bosnian refugees a week are leaving Austria to return home.

- A pre-budget summit between the government and the workers' chamber and unions takes place today, but with no agreement on how to fill the 16 billion schilling hole in the pensions. The budget is due to be announced tomorrow.
- Austrian Business Agency plans to invest 980 million schillings and create 708 jobs in Austria over the next two years.
